title: Boss: refactor a config in vim
summary: Triage a real log with :v and refactor a real nginx config with :g and :s, in real Vim.

steps.title: One file, many edits
body: The payment service paged at 02:00. You need the errors out of its log for the incident channel, and then the site config needs the change that fixes it.
Both jobs are Ex commands, the same ones you would type after `:` in full-screen Vim:
| `:v/ERROR/d` | delete every line that does **not** match |
| `:g/^\s*#/d` | delete every comment line, indented or not |
| `:g/pat/s/x/y/` | run a substitute only on lines that match `pat` |
| `:w other` then `:q!` | save the result elsewhere, leave the original |
Here you run them as `vim -es -c '...' file`.

steps.title: Only the errors
prompt: Put every `ERROR` line of `~/app.log`, in order, into `~/errors.log`. `~/app.log` itself must not change: it is evidence.
Use Vim: delete what you do not want with `:v`, write the rest to the new file, and leave without saving the log.

checks.name: errors.log has exactly the ERROR lines
checks.fail: `~/errors.log` should hold the three ERROR lines, in their original order, and nothing else.

checks.name: app.log is untouched
checks.fail: `~/app.log` changed. Write the filtered buffer with `:w ~/errors.log` and quit with `:q!`, never `:x`.

hints: `:v/ERROR/d` keeps only the matching lines in the buffer.
`:w ~/errors.log` writes the buffer to a new file; the buffer is then still "modified" against `app.log`, so leave with `:q!`.
steps.explain: `grep ERROR app.log > errors.log` does the same job, and on the shell it is the better tool. Inside Vim, `:v` and `:g` are how you do it without leaving the editor, for example on a buffer that is not a file yet (a pasted log, a command's output).

steps.title: Refactor the site config
prompt: Make `~/site.conf` ready for production, in real Vim:
1. Delete every comment line (including the indented `# TODO`).
3. The upstream `old_backend` becomes `api_backend`, but the location `/old_backend_status` keeps its name.
4. Every `proxy_pass` line ends with `;` (one of them is missing it, which is the bug that broke the reload).
Several `-c` commands in one `vim -es` run, ending with `-c x`.

checks.name: site.conf is production-ready
checks.fail: `~/site.conf` is not right yet. In the diff, `<` lines are the goal and `>` lines are yours.

checks.name: every proxy_pass line ends with ;
checks.fail: A `proxy_pass` line still has no `;` at the end.

hints: Comments: `:g/^\s*#/d`. Host: `:%s/staging\.example\.com/shop.example.com/g` (escape the dots, or they match any character).
Upstream: `:%s/\<old_backend\>/api_backend/g`. `_` counts as a word character, so `old_backend_status` is left alone.
Semicolons only on proxy_pass lines: `:g/proxy_pass/s/;\=$/;/` (`\=` means "zero or one").
steps.explain: `:g/pattern/command` is the power tool: it picks the lines, then any Ex command (`d`, `s`, `norm`, `m0`) runs on each. On a real server you would now run `sudo nginx -t` before reloading.

steps.title: Real keys: strip the comments
prompt: Last one with your own fingers: delete every comment line in one command, typed in the trainer.
steps.explain: `:g/^#/d`. Eight keys for any number of lines.
